title: Queries on Number of Points Inside a Circle
summary: Given an array of points with their coordinates and an array of circles defined by their center coordinates and radii, calculate the number of points inside each circle, including points on the circle's border.
statement: Given an array of points with their coordinates and an array of circles defined by their center coordinates and radii, calculate the number of points inside each circle, including points on the circle's border. Return an array of results corresponding to each query.
constraints: Count points on or inside each circle independently and return counts in query order.
hints: Avoid square roots by comparing squared distances.
For each query, scan all points and compute dx²+dy².
Count a point when squared distance is at most radius².
Squaring preserves nonnegative distance order, and the inclusive comparison includes both interior and boundary points exactly.
editorial: Squaring preserves nonnegative distance order, and the inclusive comparison includes both interior and boundary points exactly.

tests.explanation: The three circles contain three, two, and two points respectively.
The radius-zero circle contains its exact center; the second contains all three points.
